first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both currently declining, and prior evidence indicates onboarding and signup simplification durably improve activation and time-to-value. Promotional pricing is a credible response to the competitor but requires verification because acquisition lift may not translate to sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. This directly addresses the 4% decline in completion and the 6% activation decline, while verified evidence shows shortened onboarding increased completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention 3%. Do not use promotional pricing: although it increased qualified revenue initially, the verified cohort had 12% lower 30-day retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, making it inconsistent with sustainable qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. The deeper price cut and doubled SMB churn conversations raise an immediate competitive risk, but the only directly verified pricing evidence shows targeted discounts produced a 12% 30-day retention decline and failed to survive the first renewal cycle. That makes promotional pricing unsuitable for the primary objective of sustainable qualified revenue. Simplified onboarding has verified gains in completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, and directly addresses the concurrent declines in onboarding completion and activation. The experiment will not fully resolve acute price-driven churn, so that exposure remains flagged.
